$ grep -ciE 'password|client_secret|BEGIN .*PRIVATE' /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
0

# WHAT IS NOT IN THIS FILE
#
# No password. No client secret. No certificate. No connection string.
# `managed_identity` names a client id, and a client id is an identifier -
# it grants nothing. The VM holds the identity, so Prometheus asks the
# instance metadata service for a token and never stores one.
#
# The Entra ID auth option Microsoft also documents DOES need a client
# secret. This lab forbids those outright, which is why the managed identity
# path is the only one here.
#
# THE URL IS ASSEMBLED, NOT PASTED
#
# Host comes from the data collection ENDPOINT. Path names the data
# collection RULE by its IMMUTABLE id. Both are read back from the
# workspace after apply, so a rebuild in another subscription renders a
# correct file with nothing to hand-edit.
#
# Reading the host from the data collection RULE instead returns an EMPTY
# STRING. That renders a URL of "/dataCollectionRules/..." which applies
# cleanly, boots cleanly, and fails at runtime with
# `unsupported protocol scheme ""`. An empty string is a valid string, so
# nothing warns. vm.tf now carries a PRECONDITION on the VM that consumes
# this URL, so the VM is never created with a config that cannot work.
# Not a `check` block - a failed check is only a WARNING, and it runs
# after Terraform has already provisioned.
